intro: Lesson 24. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ فِىٓ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍۢ (٤) ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَٰهُ أَسْفَلَ سَٰفِلِينَ (٥)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: We have certainly created man in the best of stature;
Then We return him to the lowest of the low,

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Light hum, tongue near the س

questions.q: Chunk and link At-Tin 95:4-5 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 95:4-5 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: «ثُمَّ» has a meem with shaddah. We hum for ...
Listening rota: today's group recites 95:4-5 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Find the ikhfa (noon sakinah) in 95:4 and say its next letter.
In one sentence: why does Allah mention 'the lowest of the low' (95:5) after the best of stature?
questions.a: To warn that a person who turns away from faith and good deeds falls low; 95:6 gives the exception.
A) in the best of stature. 95:4: 'We have certainly created man in the best of stature.'

questions.q: At-Tin 95:4: «لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Allah says He created people 'in the best of stature'. What can your body do that shows how well it is made?
questions.a: Walk, think, speak, see, heal: every part works together. We thank Allah by using it well.
